whatItDoes: Builds a debt payoff plan from your debts, minimum payments, and a monthly budget. You can choose the snowball or avalanche strategy to see the payoff order, total months, and total interest paid, and compare which strategy finishes faster.
whyItExists: Carrying multiple debts is overwhelming, and paying minimums across every card can extend payoff for years. A simple plan that directs every extra dollar at one clear target debt shortens the timeline and shows real progress with the snowball or avalanche order.
whoShouldUse: Anyone with multiple credit cards, personal loans, student loans, or auto loans who wants a clear payoff sequence and knows what they can pay monthly.
useCases: Order debts by smallest balance (snowball) for quick wins
Order by highest APR (avalanche) to minimize interest
See how an extra monthly budget shortens the plan
Plan which card receives the surplus each month
Compare snowball vs. avalanche to choose the strategy that fits your motivation
Forecast when you will be debt-free and the total interest you'll pay
instructions: Add each debt with its name, balance, APR, and minimum payment
Set your total monthly budget for debt repayment
Choose a strategy: snowball or avalanche
Read the payoff months, total interest, and the payoff order
Switch strategies to compare timelines and interest
Increase the budget to see how much faster you finish
examples: Debt A $4,000 at 18.99% and Debt B $8,000 at 7.5%, $500/month → avalanche targets A first and saves the most interest
Three small debts with $600/month using snowball → smallest balance cleared in the first months for momentum
Two cards at 24% and 12% with a $300 budget → putting the extra $200 on the 24% card finishes faster and cheaper
bestPractices: Set the budget at least equal to the sum of the minimum payments
Keep paying minimums on every debt so nothing falls behind
Understand snowball is motivational, avalanche is interest-optimal
Re-run the plan if balances or minimums change
Automate the payment to the target debt so the plan actually happens
commonMistakes: Setting a budget below the total minimums (no plan is possible)
Entering an APR instead of a monthly rate by mistake
Forgetting zero-APR promotional balances still count
Assuming the payoff ignores interest charged during the plan
Switching strategies mid-plan and losing the momentum of early wins
faq: Is this financial advice? — No, it is a planning estimate.
Which is better, snowball or avalanche? — Avalanche saves the most interest; snowball gives faster first wins to stay motivated.
Why is there no plan? — The monthly budget must be at least the sum of the minimums.
Are my numbers sent anywhere? — No, everything runs locally in your browser.
Can I pay off debt faster than the plan? — Yes, any additional payment shortens the timeline and reduces interest further.
Should I keep saving while paying off debt? — A small emergency fund prevents new debt when surprises happen; pay minimums first, then attack the target debt.
